negative_findings.description: Neither Diebold Nixdorf's nor NCR Atleos' public case-study/customer-reference libraries surfaced any Hungary-specific bank case study in hu or en searches; CEE examples found were Czech (CSOB) and German/Nordic.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's core hypothesis (vendor reference pages expose HU bank decisions) holds only weakly for the two largest ATM OEMs; the stronger HU evidence turned out to be municipal contracts, the MNB ATM regulation and local entity accounts.

brief: Hungary's self-service and banking-IT vendor landscape is only partly visible through classic vendor reference marketing: the two largest ATM OEMs (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos) publish no Hungary-specific case study, so their HU footprint must be inferred from local legal entities (Diebold Nixdorf Kft., Vecsés, reg. 01-09-690680) and their statutory accounts. The richest public traces are elsewhere: Euronet's SEC filings and HU press room quantify the Hungarian ATM estate and name bank outsourcing deals (e.g. Budapest Bank's ~145-ATM 10-year contract), GVH proceedings expose its market conduct, and municipal council documents publish actual 'kihelyezett ATM' service contracts naming both the bank (MBH) and its ATM operating partner. Overlaying all of this, MNB decree 19/2025 assigns named banks a settlement-by-settlement ATM installation obligation with escalating fines, creating a dated, bank-attributed demand pipeline that HU financial media track article by article. On the software/integration side, 4iG's BÉT and IR disclosures and Dorsum's HU blog and Portfolio.hu interviews are the practical substitute for absent bank procurement disclosure.
